### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371, Reactome:R-HSA-6805567)

**Proposed mechanism:** KRT5 pathogenic variant —DISRUPTS→ KRT5 (HGNC:6411); KRT5 (HGNC:6411) —DISRUPTS→ keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0035203); keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0035203) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0007348); keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0035203) —LEADS_TO→ Mottled pigmentation (HP:0001012); PKP1 pathogenic variant —DISRUPTS→ PKP1 (HGNC:9145); PKP1 (HGNC:9145) —DISRUPTS→ keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0035203); keratin intermediate filament organization (GO:0035203) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency (MONDO:0011472). Pathogenic variants in KRT5 disrupt keratin intermediate filament organization, leading to epidermolysis bullosa simplex and mottled pigmentation. Similarly, pathogenic variants in PKP1 disrupt the same keratin intermediate filament organization pathway, causing epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency. Thus, both diseases converge on a shared pathway critical for epidermal structure.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in either KRT5 or PKP1 in individuals diagnosed with these respective conditions, or the identification of pathogenic variants in entirely distinct cellular pathways that do not converge on keratin intermediate filament organization, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic screening reveals that pathogenic variants associated with EBS-MP are predominantly found in KRT5 and not PKP1, and vice versa for EBS-PKP1, it would weaken the proposed mechanistic overlap. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing high allele frequencies (>1%) for pathogenic variants in KRT5 or PKP1 in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on keratin intermediate filament organization provides a potential therapeutic target for both conditions. Strategies aimed at stabilizing or restoring the function of this network, perhaps through chaperone therapy or gene therapy targeting essential components, could offer benefit to patients with either form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
